debutant.question: In which city was Jesus born?
debutant.explanation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea (Matthew 2:1).

debutant.question: How many apostles did Jesus choose?
debutant.explanation: Jesus chose 12 apostles (Matthew 10:1-4).

debutant.question: Which apostle denied Jesus three times?
debutant.explanation: Peter denied Jesus three times before the rooster crowed (Matthew 26:34).

debutant.question: What is Jesus' first miracle?
debutant.explanation: Jesus' first miracle was changing water into wine at the wedding in Cana (John 2:1-11).

debutant.question: Who baptized Jesus?
debutant.explanation: John the Baptist baptized Jesus in the Jordan River (Matthew 3:13-17).

debutant.question: What is the last book of the New Testament?
debutant.explanation: Revelation (Revelation) is the last book of the New Testament.

debutant.question: How many days did Jesus spend in the desert?
debutant.explanation: Jesus spent 40 days and 40 nights in the desert (Matthew 4:2).

debutant.question: How many loaves did Jesus use to feed 5000 people?
debutant.explanation: Jesus used 5 loaves and 2 fish to feed the crowd (John 6:9).

debutant.question: In which gospel do we find the parable of the prodigal son?
debutant.explanation: The parable of the prodigal son is found only in the Gospel of Luke (Luke 15:11-32).

debutant.question: What is the name of Jesus' mother?
debutant.explanation: Mary is the mother of Jesus (Luke 1:27).

debutant.question: Where was Jesus crucified?
debutant.explanation: Jesus was crucified at Golgotha, 'place of the skull' (John 19:17).

debutant.question: How many days after his death did Jesus resurrect?
debutant.explanation: Jesus was resurrected on the third day (1 Corinthians 15:4).

debutant.question: Which apostle was a tax collector?
debutant.explanation: Matthew (Levi) was a tax collector before following Jesus (Matthew 9:9).

debutant.question: How many gospels are there in the New Testament?
debutant.explanation: There are 4 gospels: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.

debutant.question: Who wrote the most New Testament epistles?
debutant.explanation: The apostle Paul wrote 13 epistles of the New Testament.

debutant.question: What does the dove that descended on Jesus during his baptism represent?
options: The soul of John the Baptist
debutant.explanation: The dove represents the Holy Spirit descending on Jesus at his baptism (Matthew 3:16).

debutant.question: What event is celebrated by Christians at Easter?
debutant.explanation: Easter celebrates the resurrection of Jesus Christ on the third day after his crucifixion.

debutant.question: What prayer did Jesus teach his disciples?
options: The prayer of the High Priest
debutant.explanation: Jesus taught the 'Our Father' to his disciples (Matthew 6:9-13).

debutant.question: Where was Jesus tempted by Satan?
options: On the banks of the Jordan
debutant.explanation: Jesus was tempted by Satan for 40 days in the wilderness (Matthew 4:1).

debutant.question: What is the main commandment that Jesus gives in John 13?
debutant.explanation: Jesus said 'Love one another, as I have loved you' (John 13:34).

debutant.question: In which town did Jesus grow up?
debutant.explanation: Jesus grew up in Nazareth of Galilee (Luke 2:51).

debutant.question: What was the profession of Joseph, father of Jesus?
debutant.explanation: Joseph was a carpenter (Matthew 13:55).

debutant.question: Which tree did Zacchaeus climb to see Jesus?
debutant.explanation: Zacchaeus, small in stature, had climbed a sycamore tree to see Jesus passing by (Luke 19:4).

debutant.question: How many days after his resurrection did Jesus ascend to heaven?
debutant.explanation: Jesus ascended to heaven 40 days after his resurrection (Acts 1:3).

debutant.question: What is Pentecost celebrated in the Acts of the Apostles?
options: The descent of the Holy Spirit on the disciples
The birth of the Catholic Church
debutant.explanation: Pentecost is the descent of the Holy Spirit on the disciples gathered in Jerusalem, 50 days after Easter (Acts 2).

debutant.question: What was the birth name of the Apostle Paul?
debutant.explanation: Paul's name was Saul of Tarsus before his conversion on the road to Damascus (Acts 9:1).

debutant.question: How many books are in the New Testament?
debutant.explanation: The New Testament contains 27 books.

debutant.question: What miracle did Jesus perform on his friend Lazarus?
debutant.explanation: Jesus resurrected Lazarus 4 days after his death in Bethany (John 11:43-44).

debutant.question: What title does Jesus most often use to refer to himself?
debutant.explanation: Jesus refers to himself most often as 'Son of Man' (more than 80 times in the gospels).

debutant.question: Which NT book describes Paul's missionary journeys?
debutant.explanation: The Acts of the Apostles describe Paul's 3 missionary journeys and the birth of the first Churches.

debutant.question: What is the meaning of the word 'gospel'?
debutant.explanation: The word 'gospel' comes from the Greek 'euangelion' meaning 'good news'.

debutant.question: In which gospel is the Sermon on the Mount found?
debutant.explanation: The Sermon on the Mount, including the Beatitudes and the Lord's Prayer, is found in Matthew 5-7.

debutant.question: Which apostle wrote Revelation?
debutant.explanation: Revelation was written by John on the island of Patmos (Revelation 1:1,9).

debutant.question: Which NT character sought Jesus at night for a talk about the new birth?
debutant.explanation: Nicodemus, leader of the Pharisees, came to Jesus at night to discuss the Kingdom of God (John 3:1-2).

debutant.question: What is the meaning of the word 'Christ'?
debutant.explanation: 'Christ' comes from the Greek 'Christos' meaning 'anointed', equivalent to the Hebrew word 'Messiah'.

debutant.question: What Jewish holiday did Jesus celebrate at the Last Supper?
debutant.explanation: The Last Supper was a Passover meal that Jesus celebrated with his disciples (Matthew 26:17-20).

debutant.question: What city was the center of Jesus' ministry in Galilee?
debutant.explanation: Capernaum was the base of Jesus' Galilean ministry, called 'his own city' (Matthew 9:1).

debutant.question: Which disciple of Jesus was a doctor?
debutant.explanation: Luke was a physician ('the beloved physician', Colossians 4:14) and wrote the Gospel of Luke and Acts.

debutant.question: What parable does Jesus tell to describe the different types of hearts receiving the Word?
debutant.explanation: The parable of the sower describes 4 types of ground/heart receiving God's Word differently (Matthew 13:1-23).

debutant.question: What name does Jesus give to Simon after his confession of faith?
debutant.explanation: Jesus said to Simon 'You are Peter (Kephas), and on this rock I will build my Church' (Matthew 16:18).

debutant.question: What is the central message of the Gospel?
options: Jesus died and rose again for our sins
debutant.explanation: The gospel is that Jesus Christ died for our sins, was buried, and rose again (1 Corinthians 15:3-4).

debutant.question: Who was Pontius Pilate in the Passion of Jesus?
options: The High Priest who judged Jesus
The Roman governor who sentenced Jesus to death
debutant.explanation: Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor of Judea who, although recognizing Jesus' innocence, condemned him to crucifixion (John 18:38; 19:16).

debutant.question: What symbol does Jesus use in John 15 to describe his relationship with believers?
debutant.explanation: Jesus said 'I am the vine, you are the branches' (John 15:5).

debutant.question: What is the meaning of 'Emmanuel'?
debutant.explanation: 'Immanuel' means 'God with us' (Matthew 1:23, quoting Isaiah 7:14).

debutant.question: Which country did Jesus visit as a refugee as a child?
debutant.explanation: Joseph, Mary, and the baby Jesus fled to Egypt to escape Herod's massacre (Matthew 2:13-15).

debutant.question: Which apostle wrote two NT epistles and was married?
debutant.explanation: Peter wrote two epistles (1 and 2 Peter) and was married (Matthew 8:14 mentions his mother-in-law).

debutant.question: What does the term 'apostle' mean?
options: Sent (one who is sent on a mission)
debutant.explanation: 'Apostle' comes from the Greek 'apostolos' meaning 'one who is sent'.

debutant.question: How many missionary journeys did Paul complete according to Acts?
debutant.explanation: Acts describes 3 major missionary journeys of Paul (Acts 13-14; 15-18; 18-21).

debutant.question: What does 'Pentecost' literally mean in Greek?
debutant.explanation: Pentecost comes from the Greek 'pentêkostê' meaning 'fiftieth' (Acts 2:1).

debutant.question: Which disciple asked Jesus to show him the way to the Father?
debutant.explanation: Philip said to Jesus, 'Lord, show us the Father.' Jesus responds: 'He who has seen me has seen the Father' (John 14:8-9).

debutant.question: Which episode shows Jesus as a child in the Temple in Jerusalem?
options: Jesus among the doctors at age 12
debutant.explanation: At age 12, Jesus remained in the Temple in Jerusalem among the doctors of the Law (Luke 2:41-50).

intermediaire.question: On which mountain was Jesus transfigured?
intermediaire.explanation: Tradition places the Transfiguration on Mount Tabor (Matthew 17:1-9).

intermediaire.question: Which NT character asked for the head of John the Baptist?
intermediaire.explanation: Herodias requested John the Baptist's head through his daughter (Mark 6:24-25).

intermediaire.question: In which book do we find Peter's speech at Pentecost?
intermediaire.explanation: Peter's speech at Pentecost is found in Acts 2.

intermediaire.question: Which NT woman poured perfume on Jesus' feet?
intermediaire.explanation: Mary of Bethany anointed Jesus' feet with expensive ointment (John 12:3).

intermediaire.question: What was Peter's job before following Jesus?
intermediaire.explanation: Peter was a fisherman on Lake Galilee (Matthew 4:18).

intermediaire.question: Which apostle walked on water toward Jesus?
intermediaire.explanation: Peter walked on water to join Jesus (Matthew 14:29).

intermediaire.question: What is the first epistle of Paul chronologically?
intermediaire.explanation: 1 Thessalonians is considered the oldest epistle of Paul (c. 50 AD).

intermediaire.question: Which book describes the vision of the new Jerusalem?
intermediaire.explanation: The New Jerusalem is described in Revelation 21.

intermediaire.question: Who said 'it is no longer I who live, it is Christ who lives in me'?
intermediaire.explanation: Paul writes this in Galatians 2:20.

intermediaire.question: Which NT woman was a purple merchant?
intermediaire.explanation: Lydia was a purple merchant from the city of Thyatira (Acts 16:14).

intermediaire.question: In which gospel does Jesus say 'I am the light of the world'?
intermediaire.explanation: It is in the Gospel of John that Jesus makes the statements 'I am...' (John 8:12).

intermediaire.question: Which disciple was chosen to replace Judas among the Twelve?
intermediaire.explanation: Matthias was chosen by lot to replace Judas (Acts 1:26).

intermediaire.question: Who is the first Christian martyr mentioned in Acts?
intermediaire.explanation: Stephen was the first Christian martyr, stoned to death after his speech before the Sanhedrin (Acts 7:59).

intermediaire.question: In which city were Paul and Silas imprisoned before an earthquake opened the gates?
intermediaire.explanation: In Philippi, an earthquake opened the prison doors (Acts 16:26).

intermediaire.question: What parable does Jesus tell to explain who our neighbor is?
options: The parable of the Good Samaritan
The Parable of the Lost Sheep
intermediaire.explanation: The parable of the Good Samaritan answers 'Who is my neighbor?' (Luke 10:25-37).

intermediaire.question: What event marks the beginning of the Church according to Acts?
intermediaire.explanation: Pentecost, with the outpouring of the Holy Spirit, is the starting point of the Church (Acts 2).

intermediaire.question: What is special about the Gospel of John compared to the three synoptics?
options: It does not contain parables but revealing signs and speeches
He is the only one to mention the resurrection
intermediaire.explanation: John differs from the synoptics: no parables in the strict sense, but 7 miraculous 'signs' and 7 major 'I am' declarations revealing the divine identity of Jesus.

intermediaire.question: What theological concept does Paul mainly develop in the epistle to the Romans?
intermediaire.explanation: The book of Romans is the great exposition of justification by faith (Romans 1-8).

intermediaire.question: What is the main doctrine of the epistle to the Hebrews?
options: The superiority of the priesthood of Christ over the Levitical priesthood
intermediaire.explanation: The epistle to the Hebrews demonstrates the superiority of Christ as high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.

intermediaire.question: Which apostle refused to believe in the resurrection before seeing and touching Jesus?
intermediaire.explanation: Thomas said 'Except I see in his hands the mark of the nails...I will not believe' (John 20:25).

intermediaire.question: What was the main problem that Paul addresses in Galatians?
options: The false doctrine that circumcision and the Law of Moses were necessary for salvation
intermediaire.explanation: Paul fights in Galatians the 'Judaizers' who taught that faith in Christ was not enough.

intermediaire.question: What major decision did the Council of Jerusalem (Acts 15) make?
options: The list of canonical books of the NT
Gentiles do not need to be circumcised to be saved
The election of the first bishop of Rome
The ban on marriage for pastors
intermediaire.explanation: The Council of Jerusalem decided that Gentiles did not need to be circumcised to be saved (Acts 15).

intermediaire.question: What is the theological meaning of the term 'redemption' in the NT?
options: The Redemption of a Slave by the Payment of a Price — Christ has redeemed us by his blood
The moral transformation of the believer
intermediaire.explanation: Redemption (apolytrosis) literally means the redemption of a slave—Christ has redeemed us at a price (1 Corinthians 6:20).

intermediaire.question: What is the content of the hymn to Christ in Philippians 2:6-11 (kenosis)?
options: The voluntary abasement of Christ and his exaltation by God
intermediaire.explanation: The hymn of Philippians 2:6-11 describes kenosis: Christ 'emptied himself' by taking the form of a servant, and then God exalted him.

intermediaire.question: What is the main subject of the epistle of James?
intermediaire.explanation: James emphasizes that faith without works is dead (James 2:17).

intermediaire.question: What is the connection between the Lord's Supper and Passover in NT theology?
options: The Last Supper fulfills and replaces the Jewish Passover — Christ is the Passover Lamb
The Last Supper is entirely new with no connection to the OT
Passover and the Last Supper are unrelated parallel rites
intermediaire.explanation: Paul says 'Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed' (1 Corinthians 5:7). The Last Supper is the fulfillment of the Passover.

intermediaire.question: What Christological doctrine is condemned by John in his epistles (docetism)?
options: That Jesus was a simple man
That Jesus did not come in the flesh — denying the actual incarnation
That Jesus is inferior to the Father
intermediaire.explanation: Jean fights Docetism. 1 John 4:2: 'Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God.'

intermediaire.question: Which apostle was the first to recognize that the gospel extended to non-Jews (Gentiles)?
intermediaire.explanation: Peter received a vision of the cloth with unclean animals and was sent to the centurion Cornelius—the first baptism of a Gentile (Acts 10).

intermediaire.question: What is the difference between 'justification' and 'sanctification' in Pauline theology?
options: Justification is the legal act of God declaring us righteous; sanctification is the process of transformation in Christ
Justification comes from our works; the sanctification of faith
The justification is final; sanctification is impossible
intermediaire.explanation: Justification is an instantaneous act of God declaring the sinner righteous. Sanctification is the ongoing process of transformation.

intermediaire.question: What is the content of Jesus' great priestly prayer in John 17?
options: Prayer for healing of the sick
Prayer for the glory of the Father, the protection of the disciples and the unity of all believers
intermediaire.explanation: John 17: for his own glorification (v.1-5), for his disciples (v.6-19) and for all future believers (v.20-26).

intermediaire.question: Which NT text describes the 'fruit of the Spirit' in 9 characteristics?
intermediaire.explanation: Galatians 5:22-23 lists the 9 fruits of the Spirit: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control.

intermediaire.question: What is the problem that Paul addresses in 1st Corinthians?
options: Divisions in the Church, Immorality, Misused Spiritual Gifts
intermediaire.explanation: 1 Corinthians addresses multiple issues: factions, immorality, marriage, sacrificed meat, worship and giving, resurrection.

intermediaire.question: What is the meaning of the term 'grace' (charis) in NT theology?
options: Unmerited divine favor freely granted by God for salvation
The moral beauty of the believer
intermediaire.explanation: 'Charis' is divine grace—the absolutely free and unmerited favor of God (Ephesians 2:8-9).

intermediaire.question: What is the central theme of the epistle to the Hebrews expressed by the repetition of 'best' (kreittôn)?
options: The superiority of the Church over Israel
The absolute superiority of Christ and the new covenant over all that has gone before
The superiority of the Jews over the Gentiles
The superiority of Paul over the other apostles
intermediaire.explanation: The Epistle to the Hebrews uses 'kreittôn' (better) 13 times: better name, better alliance, better promises, better sacrifice.

intermediaire.question: What is the unique contribution of Luke's gospel to NT theology?
options: Emphasis on the divinity of Christ
Emphasis on prayer, the Holy Spirit, women, the poor and the universal scope of salvation
intermediaire.explanation: Luke is distinguished by: the centrality of prayer, the Holy Spirit, the marginalized (women, poor, sinners, Samaritans, Gentiles).

intermediaire.question: What is the meaning of the term 'incarnation' in NT Christology?
options: The Eternal Son of God Taking Full Human Nature
The human appearance of God in the OT
intermediaire.explanation: The incarnation refers to the act by which the eternal Son of God took on a full human nature in John 1:14: 'The Word was made flesh.'

intermediaire.question: What is the relationship between 'law' and 'gospel' in Pauline theology?
options: Law and gospel are the same
The Law reveals sin and leads to Christ; the Gospel announces free grace
The Law replaces the Gospel in the NT
The Gospel completely abolishes the Law without remainder
intermediaire.explanation: Paul: 'The law is our teacher to bring us to Christ' (Galatians 3:24). The Law accuses, the Gospel liberates.

intermediaire.question: What is the meaning of the 'New Covenant' established by Jesus at the Last Supper?
options: The fulfillment of Jeremiah 31:31-34: forgiveness of sins, law in the hearts, direct access to God through the blood of Christ
The creation of a new religion separate from Judaism
A conditional covenant based on our obedience
intermediaire.explanation: Jesus said 'This cup is the new covenant in my blood' (Luke 22:20) — fulfilling the promise of Jeremiah 31:31-34.

expert.question: What Greek term refers to the second coming of Christ in the epistles?
expert.explanation: The Greek term 'Parousia' (παρουσία) refers to the second coming of Christ (1 Thessalonians 4:15).

expert.question: In Revelation 2-3, how many churches does Jesus address?
expert.explanation: Jesus addresses his messages to 7 Churches in Asia Minor (Revelation 2-3).

expert.question: What Pauline theological term means 'reconciliation by substitution'?
expert.explanation: 'Propitation' (ἱλαστήριον) refers to the act which appeases God's righteous wrath (Romans 3:25).

expert.question: According to Paul in Ephesians, what is the Church founded on?
options: Apostles and prophets, with Christ as the cornerstone
expert.explanation: The Church is founded on the apostles and prophets, with Christ being the cornerstone (Ephesians 2:20).

expert.question: In John 1, what Greek term is translated 'Word'?
expert.explanation: John uses 'Logos' (λόγος) to refer to Christ (John 1:1).

expert.question: Which city is cryptically referred to as 'Babylon' in 1 Peter 5:13?
expert.explanation: Historians agree that 'Babylon' in 1 Peter 5:13 refers to Rome.

expert.question: In Hebrews 7, to what priestly order is the priesthood of Christ compared?
expert.explanation: Christ is declared 'high priest according to the order of Melchizedek' (Hebrews 7:17).

expert.question: What is the meaning of the term 'Abba' in Romans 8:15?
expert.explanation: 'Abba' is the affectionate Aramaic term for 'Father', equivalent to 'Daddy'.

expert.question: In Revelation, what is the number of the 'Beast'?
expert.explanation: The number of the Beast is 666 (Revelation 13:18).

expert.question: What doctrine affirms that the two natures of Christ coexist without mixture or confusion?
expert.explanation: The Council of Chalcedon (451) defined the two complete natures of Christ.

expert.question: On which hill did Paul deliver his speech to the Athenians (Acts 17)?
expert.explanation: Paul delivered his speech on the Areopagus in Athens (Acts 17:22).

expert.question: What NT Greek term describes the gathering of the Christian Church?
expert.explanation: 'Ekklesia' (ἐκκλησία) means 'assembly of the called out'.

expert.question: In Pauline theology, what is 'justification by faith' (dikaiôsis)?
options: A divine legal act by which the sinner is declared righteous
expert.explanation: For Paul, justification is a legal act (forensic) by which God declares the sinner righteous on the basis of faith in Christ.

expert.question: What central Johannine concept describes the 'dwelling' of Christ in the believer?
expert.explanation: The verb 'menein' (μένειν, remain) is central in John 15:4-7 and 1 John 4:16.

expert.question: What hypothetical source designates the material common to Matthew and Luke, absent from Mark?
expert.explanation: The 'Q source' (from the German Quelle = source) is a hypothetical source of Jesus' sayings.

expert.question: What is the main issue of the 'synoptic problem' in biblical theology?
options: Why there are 4 gospels and not just one
How to explain the similarities and differences between Matthew, Mark and Luke
The authenticity of the gospel of John
The date of composition of the gospels
expert.explanation: The 'synoptic problem' deals with the literary dependence between Matthew, Mark and Luke.

expert.question: What is the theological meaning of the term 'atonement' (hilasmos) in 1 John 2:2?
options: The act by which Christ satisfies divine justice and appeases the wrath of God for our sins
expert.explanation: 'Hilasmos' means 'propitiation' — the act by which Christ fulfills the requirements of divine holiness (1 John 2:2; 4:10; Romans 3:25).

expert.question: What is the structure of Jesus' 'Apocalyptic Discourse' in Matthew 24-25?
options: A simple list of chronological signs
An answer to two questions (destruction of the Temple / sign of the Parousia) with a double prophetic perspective
An allegory on the life of the Church
expert.explanation: Matthew 24-25 answers the disciples' questions about the destruction of the Temple AND the final Parousia, intertwining the two horizons.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the term 'kenosis' in Pauline Christology (Philippians 2:7)?
options: The self-emptying of the Son—he renounced the independent exercise of certain divine attributes by incarnating
expert.explanation: Kenosis (κένωσις): the Son of God 'emptied himself' (ekénôsen) by taking the form of a servant (Philippians 2:7).

expert.question: What is the difference between 'rhema' and 'logos' in the Greek NT?
options: 'Logos' means the immutable divine Word (John 1:1); 'rhemah' refers to a specific word spoken (Romans 10:17)
'Logos' is the NT, 'rhema' is the OT
'Logos' is the teaching, 'rhema' is the prophecy
expert.explanation: 'Logos' tends towards the overall divine Word, 'rhema' towards a specific spoken word. Romans 10:17: 'Faith comes by hearing.'

expert.question: What is the significance of the statement 'Before Abraham was, I Am' (John 8:58)?
options: A claim to absolute divine identity: the divine name 'I Am' (YHWH, Exodus 3:14) applies to Christ
A simple sign of spiritual greatness
expert.explanation: John 8:58: 'Ego eimi' refers directly to the divine name YHWH ('I am he who am', Exodus 3:14). The Jews seeking to stone him confirm that they understood the divine claim.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the term 'metanoia' (repentance) in the gospels in relation to simple regret?
options: A radical change in mental, spiritual, and practical orientation—existential turn toward God
The simple admission of one's faults
expert.explanation: 'Metanoia' (meta = change + noein = think) designates a radical and total change of existential direction. John the Baptist and Jesus proclaim metanoia as a condition of entry into the Kingdom.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the term 'propitiation' (hilastêrion) in Romans 3:25 and how it relates to the OT?
options: The 'mercy seat' or mercy seat of the Ark — Jesus is its fulfillment in his own person
A Greek philosophical term unrelated to the OT
expert.explanation: Romans 3:25 uses 'hilastêrion' — the same term as the LXX for the 'kapporeth' (cover of the Ark). God publicly presented Christ as THIS place of propitiation.

expert.question: What is the Trinitarian baptismal formula of Matthew 28:19 and its dogmatic significance?
options: Three separate baptisms for each divine person
A single baptism in a single Trinitarian 'Name' (singular) — testifying to the unity and tripersonality of God
A liturgical formula without dogmatic significance
expert.explanation: Matthew 28:19: 'in the name' (eis to onoma, singular) of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit - the singular 'name' testifies to the divine unity in the threefold personal distinction.

expert.question: What is the significance of the image of the 'Lamb of God' (John 1:29) in sacrificial theology?
options: Convergence between the Passover lamb (Exodus 12), the Suffering Servant (Isaiah 53:7), daily sacrifices and the Lamb of the Apocalypse
A reference to the scapegoat of Leviticus 16
expert.explanation: The image of the lamb in John 1:29 is a typological convergence: paschal lamb, Suffering Servant, daily sacrifice, and the Lamb of the Apocalypse.

expert.question: What is the meaning of 'telos' in Matthew 5:48 ('be ye perfect as your heavenly Father is perfect')?
options: 'Telos' = complete, accomplished, mature — call for maturity and integrity in love
A Platonic ideal of moral excellence
expert.explanation: 'Teleios' comes from 'telos' (goal, accomplishment) — not flawless perfection, but maturation and accomplished love. The context is about loving your enemies as God loves all.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the baptismal formula 'in the name of the Father, of the Son and of the Holy Spirit' in Trinitarian theology?
options: A single baptism in a single Trinitarian 'Name' (singular) — testifying to the unity and tripersonality of God
A liturgical formula without dogmatic significance
A post-apostolic development absent from the primitive NT
expert.explanation: Matthew 28:19: 'in the name' (singular) testifies to the divine unity in the threefold personal distinction. This verse is one of the foundations of the Trinitarian doctrine.

expert.question: What is the cosmic significance of the reconciliation in Colossians 1:20?
options: Only the reconciliation of human beings with God
The reconciliation of 'all things' — heaven and earth — through the blood of Christ
The apocatastasis (universal salvation of all beings)
The pacification of human conflicts only
expert.explanation: Colossians 1:20 states that God has purposed to 'reconcile all things to himself through Christ.' Redemption has cosmic significance.

expert.question: What is the meaning of the 'resurrection of the body' as a Christian hope distinct from the Platonic immortality of the soul?
options: Resurrection involves the rehabilitation of the whole person, body and soul; Platonic immortality frees the soul from the body
Resurrection is simply the survival of the soul
Resurrection is not taught in the NT consistently
expert.explanation: Christian resurrection involves the rehabilitation of the whole person. The body is not a prison but a good creation destined for glorious transformation (1 Corinthians 15:35-54).

expert.question: What is the meaning of 'mystery' (mustêrion) in Paul in Ephesians 3:6?
options: An esoteric secret reserved for initiates
What was hidden in ages past and now revealed: Gentile joint heirs with Israel in the one Body of Christ
expert.explanation: 'Mustêrion' in Paul designates a progressively accomplished divine revelation: 'the nations are joint heirs, members of the same body' (Ephesians 3:6).

expert.question: What is the theology of the Holy Spirit developed in John 14-16?
options: Spirit is a divine impersonal force
The Holy Spirit is the third divine person: Comforter, Spirit of truth, convicter of sin and righteousness
The Spirit is an intermediary angel
The Spirit is a metaphor for prophetic inspiration only
expert.explanation: John 14-16 reveals the Paraclete as a divine person: he teaches (14:26), testifies (15:26), convicts of sin (16:8), and glorifies Christ (16:14).

expert.question: What is the meaning of 'double imputation' in Reformed NT soteriology?
options: Two sins attributed to the same individual
The sin of all imputed to Christ, and the righteousness of Christ imputed to believers
Justification and sanctification as two separate acts
expert.explanation: Double imputation: (1) the sins of believers are imputed to Christ (2 Corinthians 5:21) and (2) the perfect righteousness of Christ is imputed to believers through faith (Romans 5:17).

expert.question: What is the meaning of the concept of 'union with Christ' (in Christô) which appears more than 160 times in Paul?
options: The mystical and real union of the believer with the person of the resurrected Christ, foundation of all Christian life
Conformity to the teachings of Jesus
expert.explanation: 'In Christô' (160+ occurrences): the mystical, vital and real union of the believer with the resurrected Christ - the basis of justification, sanctification, adoption and glorification.
